text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the June 28 edition of Russian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The struggle for Tyumen's oil has taken a personal turn, the paper says.
- Russia's leading libraries, which are in a state of decline, have not recieved state financing and cannot afford to subscribe for periodicals.

- The political future of rebellious general Lev Rokhlin, who attacked military policy in an address to President Boris Yeltsin, will be decided on June 30 at a meeting of activists of the political movement the general belongs to.
- The government's sequestration plans threaten the future of "Children of Russia" social programme which was earlier supported by the President, the paper says.
